basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 14.' and it opens 'Vers. 14. Et ait Dominus ad serpentem: Quia fecisti hoc, maledictus eris inter omnia'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 14. Et ait Dominus ad serpentem: Quia fecisti hoc, maledictus eris inter omnia animantia. Quod serpenti dicitur ad diabolum est referendum. Supra pectus tuum gradieris. Diabolus supra pectus graditur, quia dolos et insidias portans in pectore homines decipere conatur. Unde et merito serpens vocatur, quia occulte serpit. Terram comedit, quia terrenis operibus pascitur et delectatur.
